items.definition: To become weaker or less strong, as a storm, pain or anger does over time.
items.example: The storm finally abated just before midnight.
items.picture_idea: Dark storm clouds thinning out as the sun breaks through over a calm sea
items.definition_previous: to become less strong or intense

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: become less in amount or intensity

items.definition: To agree to something, often without wanting to, and without arguing any more.
items.example: After a long argument, she reluctantly acquiesced to her brother's plan.
items.definition_previous: to agree or give in without protest

items.definition: Having mixed feelings about something, so you cannot decide what you think of it.
items.example: Voters remain ambivalent about the proposed tax changes.
items.picture_idea: A person standing at a fork in the road, looking back and forth between two signs
items.definition_previous: having mixed or conflicting feelings about something

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: uncertain or unable to decide about what course to follow

items.definition: Very hard and tiring, and needing a lot of effort over a long time.
items.example: They began the arduous climb to the summit before dawn.
items.picture_idea: A hiker struggling up a steep, rocky mountain path with a heavy backpack
items.definition_previous: very difficult and tiring, needing a lot of effort

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: characterized by effort to the point of exhaustion; especially physical effort

items.definition: Very bold, willing to take big risks or to ignore what others think is proper.
items.example: The thieves carried out an audacious robbery in broad daylight.
items.definition_previous: bold and willing to take risks, sometimes rudely so

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: disposed to venture or take risks

items.definition: Kind and generous, and wanting to help other people.
items.example: A benevolent donor paid for the new children's wing of the hospital.
items.picture_idea: An elderly man handing a bag of food to a smiling family
items.definition_previous: kind, generous and wanting to help others

items.definition: To make something stronger or more secure by giving it extra support.
items.example: The good news helped bolster confidence in the economy.
items.definition_previous: to support or strengthen something

items.definition: Being short, especially in speech or writing, by using only a few words.
items.explanation: Also used for something lasting only a short time.
items.example: The speech was praised for its brevity and clarity.
items.definition_previous: the quality of being short, especially in speech or writing

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: the attribute of being brief or fleeting

items.definition: Honest and open in what you say, even when the truth is hard to hear.
items.example: In a candid interview, the coach admitted the team had played badly.
items.picture_idea: Two people talking frankly across a table
items.definition_previous: honest and direct, even when the truth is uncomfortable

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: openly straightforward and direct without reserve or secretiveness

items.definition: Changing suddenly and for no clear reason, like a person's mood or the weather.
items.example: The capricious weather ruined our plans for the picnic.
items.definition_previous: changing suddenly and without clear reason in mood or behavior

items.definition: Careful, and thinking about possible risks before you say or do something.
items.example: The minister was circumspect when reporters asked about the deal.
items.definition_previous: careful to think about possible risks before acting

items.definition: Kept secret, often because other people would not allow it or would not approve.
items.example: The two leaders held a clandestine meeting in a small hotel.
items.picture_idea: Two figures in coats whispering in a dark alley at night
items.definition_previous: done in secret, often because it is not allowed

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: conducted with or marked by hidden aims or methods

items.definition: Clear and logical, so that people find it easy to believe.
items.example: She made a cogent argument for building the new library.
items.definition_previous: clear, logical and convincing

items.definition: A confusing problem or question that is very hard to solve.
items.example: The city faces a conundrum: it needs more housing but has no land.
items.picture_idea: A person scratching their head in front of a tangled maze
items.definition_previous: a confusing problem or question that is hard to solve

items.definition: To end at the highest or most important point, after things have built up over time.
items.example: Months of protests culminated in a huge march through the capital.
items.definition_previous: to reach a final or highest point

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: end, especially to reach a final or climactic stage

items.definition: A serious lack of something, when there is far too little of it.
items.example: There is a dearth of affordable apartments in the city.
items.picture_idea: An almost empty shelf in a shop
items.definition_previous: a serious lack or shortage of something

items.definition: A sudden and complete failure that is very embarrassing or causes great trouble.
items.example: The company's product launch turned into a public debacle.
items.definition_previous: a total and embarrassing failure

items.definition: To make someone decide not to do something, by making it seem hard or risky.
items.example: High prices may deter tourists from visiting the island.
items.definition_previous: to make someone decide not to do something

items.definition: Working hard and carefully, and not giving up on a task.
items.example: The diligent student checked every answer twice.
items.picture_idea: A student studying carefully at a desk with books and notes
items.definition_previous: working hard and carefully

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: characterized by care and perseverance in carrying out tasks

items.definition: Strong disagreement with an idea or decision that most people or leaders accept.
items.explanation: Also a verb meaning to disagree.
items.example: There was growing dissent among workers after the new rules were announced.
items.definition_previous: disagreement with an official or commonly held opinion
items.example_previous: The judge wrote a dissent explaining why she disagreed with the ruling.

items.definition: Able to speak or write clearly and in a way that moves people.
items.example: The mayor gave an eloquent speech after the flood.
items.picture_idea: A speaker addressing a crowd from a podium
items.definition_previous: able to speak or write clearly and persuasively

items.definition: Hard to find or catch, because it keeps getting away.
items.example: The elusive thief has avoided police for months.
items.picture_idea: A fox slipping away between trees, barely seen
items.definition_previous: hard to find, catch or achieve

items.definition: To make a story more interesting by adding extra details, often ones that are not true.
items.example: He liked to embellish his stories with imaginary adventures.
items.definition_previous: to make something more interesting by adding details, often untrue ones

items.definition: Lasting only a short time before it fades or disappears.
items.example: Fame can be ephemeral, fading as quickly as it arrived.
items.picture_idea: A soap bubble about to pop
items.definition_previous: lasting only a very short time

items.definition: To make a problem or bad situation even worse.
items.example: The drought was exacerbated by a record-breaking heat wave.
items.definition_previous: to make a problem or bad situation worse

items.definition: Very careful about small details and cleanliness, and hard to please.
items.example: She was fastidious about keeping her desk perfectly tidy.
items.picture_idea: A neat desk with pens lined up in a perfect row
items.definition_previous: very careful about details and hard to please

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: giving careful attention to detail; hard to please; excessively concerned with cleanliness

items.definition: Showing very strong and sincere feeling or belief.
items.example: He was a fervent supporter of the local team.
items.picture_idea: A fan cheering passionately in a stadium wearing a team scarf
items.definition_previous: showing strong and sincere feeling or belief

items.definition: To grow well and be healthy or successful.
items.example: Small businesses flourished after the new market opened.
items.picture_idea: A garden full of healthy, blooming flowers
items.definition_previous: to grow or develop well and be successful

items.definition: To help something grow or get stronger over time.
items.explanation: Also means to care for a child who is not your own for a period of time.
items.example: Good teachers foster a love of reading in their students.
items.definition_previous: to help something develop or grow over time

items.definition: Careful with money and not wasting things.
items.example: Her frugal habits allowed her to save enough for a small house.
items.picture_idea: A person counting coins and putting them into a piggy bank
items.definition_previous: careful about spending money and avoiding waste

items.definition: Having no chance of working; pointless, because it brings no result.
items.example: Their attempts to stop the flood were futile.
items.picture_idea: A person trying to sweep back ocean waves with a broom
items.definition_previous: having no chance of success; pointless

items.definition: Liking to be around other people and to talk and spend time with them.
items.example: He was a gregarious man who knew everyone in the village.
items.picture_idea: A smiling person chatting with a large group at a party
items.definition_previous: enjoying being with other people; sociable

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: instinctively or temperamentally seeking and enjoying the company of others

items.definition: A reason to complain because you feel you were treated unfairly.
items.example: The workers filed a formal grievance about unpaid overtime.
items.definition_previous: a real or imagined reason to complain about unfair treatment

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a complaint about a (real or imaginary) wrong that causes resentment and is grounds for action

items.definition: To make it hard for someone or something to move or make progress.
items.explanation: Also a noun meaning a large basket with a lid.
items.example: Heavy snow hampered rescue efforts in the mountains.
items.definition_previous: to make it hard for someone to move or progress

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: prevent the progress or free movement of

items.definition: Done without order or planning, as if left to chance.
items.example: Boxes were stacked in a haphazard way along the hall.
items.picture_idea: A messy pile of boxes stacked unevenly
items.definition_previous: lacking order or planning; random

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: dependent upon or characterized by chance

items.definition: Too much pride and self-confidence, which often leads to trouble.
items.example: The king's hubris led him to ignore every warning.
items.definition_previous: extreme pride and self-confidence that often leads to a downfall

items.definition: Fair, and not taking one side over the other.
items.example: A judge must remain impartial throughout the trial.
items.picture_idea: A set of balanced scales
items.definition_previous: fair and not favoring one side over another

items.definition: Going on and on without stopping, often in an annoying way.
items.example: The incessant noise from the building site kept us awake.
items.definition_previous: continuing without stopping, often in an annoying way

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: uninterrupted in time and indefinitely long continuing

items.definition: Certain to happen and impossible to stop or avoid.
items.example: With so little money left, closing the shop seemed inevitable.
items.definition_previous: certain to happen and impossible to avoid

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: incapable of being avoided or prevented

items.definition: Not harmful, and not likely to upset or offend anyone.
items.example: It seemed an innocuous question, but it made him nervous.
items.definition_previous: not harmful or likely to offend

items.definition: To put something at risk of being harmed, lost or spoiled.
items.example: Cutting funds could jeopardize the whole research project.
items.definition_previous: to put something at risk of harm or failure

items.definition: A point in time when something important is about to be decided or to change.
items.explanation: Also means a place where things join.
items.example: At this juncture, the talks could either succeed or collapse.
items.definition_previous: a particular point in time, especially a critical one

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a crisis situation or point in time when a critical decision must be made

items.definition: To start a feeling or interest in someone; also, to light a fire.
items.example: The teacher's stories kindled a passion for history in the class.
items.picture_idea: A small flame starting on dry twigs
items.definition_previous: to light a fire, or to awaken a feeling or interest

items.definition: To say or show that you are very sad or sorry about something.
items.explanation: Also a noun meaning a song or poem of grief.
items.example: Residents lamented the closing of the old cinema.
items.definition_previous: to express sadness or regret about something

items.definition: Not strict, especially when punishing someone; going easy on people.
items.example: Many people thought the sentence was too lenient.
items.definition_previous: less strict than expected, especially in punishing

items.definition: Bringing in a lot of money; very profitable.
items.example: She turned down a lucrative job offer to work for a charity.
items.picture_idea: A briefcase overflowing with banknotes
items.definition_previous: producing a lot of money; very profitable

items.definition: Very careful about small details and getting everything exactly right.
items.example: The detective kept meticulous notes on every clue.
items.picture_idea: A watchmaker examining tiny parts through a magnifying glass
items.definition_previous: showing great attention to detail; very careful and precise

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: marked by extreme care in treatment of details

items.definition: To make something less serious, harmful or painful.
items.explanation: Often confused with 'militate'; mitigate means to lessen.
items.example: Planting trees can help mitigate the effects of flooding.
items.definition_previous: to make something less harmful or severe

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: lessen or to try to lessen the seriousness or extent of

items.definition: Unhappy and bad-tempered, and not wanting to talk to other people.
items.example: He sat in morose silence at the end of the table.
items.picture_idea: A frowning man sitting alone with his head in his hands
items.definition_previous: gloomy, bad-tempered and unwilling to talk
